title: Emergency patch lifecycle and automated backport matrix
creator: Ava Chen
description: Goal: Define and implement an operationally simple, auditable emergency patch lifecycle that ties severity criteria to automated branch creation and a backport matrix generator. Scope: rollout gates, severity decision matrix, automated creation of patch/backport branches, CI gating for backports, telemetry checks for canary/rollback, and runbook integration. Deliverables: 1) Severity decision table mapping incident types to patch paths (patch-only vs. point-release vs. rollback). 2) A GitHub Action that generates the backport matrix (target versions and branch names) from release metadata and opens templated PRs. 3) CI job templates for backport testing and pre-merge smoke (runtime/console/upgrade). 4) Runbook update and a lightweight dashboard that surfaces candidate rollbacks and patch status. Success criteria: - Time from incident to templated backport PRs <= 60 minutes in test environment. - Backport PR CI checks pass in < 30 minutes for critical patches. - Clear, repeatable rollback path documented and validated in a dry-run. Acceptance criteria: - Merged implementation that can create patch branches for at least three active LTS tracks (1.18, 1.19, 1.20). - Automated backport matrix respects binary-compatibility and schema-change flags. - Runbook updated and reviewed by oncall, release, and security owners. Constraints and trade-offs: - We will not attempt automatic code merge for conflicts; PRs will be opened and assigned to owners. - Full automation for complex schema migrations deferred to follow-up. - Security-reviewed patches require manual approval gate before backport PRs are merged. Notes on uniqueness: this ticket centers on the automated matrix and CI-level gating rather than generic rollback playbooks. It ties release metadata (git tags, version-support-matrix) to decision logic to reduce human error.

steps: 1) Triage: determine severity using the decision table in Confluence.
2) If severity >= Sev2: run GH Action to generate backport matrix and open templated PRs.
3) Attach incident context to each PR and assign owners by component label.
4) CI gating: run backport-check.yml which runs smoke + critical SLO tests.
5) Canary rollout: deploy patch to 1% traffic, monitor telemetry, then continue to 10% and 100% if thresholds met.

6) Rollback criteria: explicit SLO breach (>0.5% error rate increase sustained for 2 minutes) or a critical data-loss signal; automated rollback script will revert patch branch and trigger emergency release for affected track.
7) Postmortem: tag incident and link to backport PRs; certify backports were necessary and document follow-up engineering tasks.
8) Dry-run cadence: perform quarterly dry-runs across all supported LTS tracks and rotate ownership during drills.
